summary: An immersive storytelling web application that archives, visualizes, and humanizes NASA’s discarded equipment across the Moon and Mars, transforming cold metallic relics into enduring testaments of human curiosity.
details:
Abandoned, But Not Forgotten

Preserving the Legacy of Humanity's Robotic Explorers Space exploration is often remembered through historic arrivals, groundbreaking discoveries, and human achievements. Yet, scattered across the Moon and Mars, countless robotic explorers remain behind as silent witnesses to humanity's journey into space. Abandoned, But Not Forgotten is an interactive digital space heritage experience that brings these forgotten spacecraft and exploration artifacts back into the spotlight. By combining historical mission data, engineering telemetry, environmental simulations, and immersive storytelling, the project explores what happens to humanity's robotic emissaries long after their missions end. The experience transforms space exploration history into an engaging journey through science, technology, memory, and preservation. Key Features 1. Interactive Dual-World Reconnaissance Radar An interactive topographic exploration interface featuring historical lunar and Martian landing sites. Users can discover the locations of significant space exploration artifacts through interactive markers and pulsing landing beacons. 2. Eight Curated Historical Pioneers Explore eight historic spacecraft and mission artifacts through dedicated historical profiles, mission records, and engineering insights: - Apollo 15 LRV-1 - Surveyor 3 - Apollo EASEP - Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity - Ingenuity Mars Helicopter - Viking 1 - InSight Lander - Perseverance Rover's Backshell Each profile highlights the engineering legacy and human stories associated with these missions, including Charlie Duke's family photograph left on the Moon, Opportunity's final farewell song, and the Wright Flyer fabric carried aboard Ingenuity. 3. Environmental Aging Simulator (2026–2126+) An interactive simulation illustrating how extraterrestrial environments may transform these artifacts over decades and centuries. It explores three major environmental processes: - Solar ultraviolet radiation and material degradation. - Micrometeorite impacts and surface pitting. - Martian dust accumulation and storm-related weathering. Users can explore projected changes over time and understand the long-term challenges of preserving human-made objects beyond Earth. 4. DSN Audio & Telemetry Decoder An immersive audio experience inspired by Deep Space Network communications. Custom Web Audio API synthesizers generate deep-space carrier-wave harmonics, accompanied by typewriter-style playback of historical spacecraft transmissions and final mission communications. 5. Send a Thought Skyward – Interactive Tribute Wall A participatory digital memorial where visitors can leave personal messages addressed to a selected rover, lander, or spacecraft. Each message is represented by a glowing golden starlight lantern released into a virtual night sky, creating a shared space for reflection and remembrance. 6. Space Heritage Policy Explorer An educational section exploring the importance of preserving humanity's extraterrestrial heritage. It introduces the 1967 Outer Space Treaty and NASA's planetary heritage preservation efforts, encouraging visitors to consider the scientific, cultural, and historical significance of space artifacts. Our Vision These spacecraft were designed to explore, discover, and communicate. Although their missions eventually ended, their contributions did not. Abandoned, But Not Forgotten aims to change how we perceive the remains of space exploration—not as discarded machines, but as historical landmarks, engineering achievements, and lasting symbols of human curiosity. Because even when our robotic explorers fall silent, their stories deserve to survive.
